create.name: Vedanta Society of Sacramento
create.bio:
The Vedanta Society of Sacramento is a branch centre of the Ramakrishna Order, set on seven wooded acres in Carmichael, a suburb of Sacramento, California. It began with local people who travelled to the San Francisco temple in the late 1940s; Swami Ashokananda asked for a centre of their own, land was bought in 1950, and monks and lay volunteers built a chapel, dedicated in 1953, then a larger auditorium, a monastery and gardens with a pond and a shrine to Shankara. Swami Shraddhananda taught here from 1957, and Swami Prapannananda has led the society since 1996, joined in 2026 by Swami Medhananda, a monk who also writes on philosophy.

The teaching follows Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi and Swami Vivekananda: the oneness of existence, the harmony of religions and the four yogas of knowledge, devotion, meditation and selfless work. Each week there is Sunday worship with a talk, evening classes on scripture, and a Thursday course on the Bhagavad Gita that people can join on Zoom or watch live. Hundreds of talks and class series are kept on its YouTube channel and in a lecture archive, and a bookshop opens at weekends.

free_resources.title: Bhagavad Gita in the Light of Sri Ramakrishna (online course)
free_resources.description: A weekly Thursday evening class with Swami Medhananda reading the Gita through Ramakrishna's teaching, with Sri Aurobindo's essays as the textbook. Join on Zoom or follow live on YouTube; earlier course series such as the Katha and Mundaka Upanishads are linked as playlists.

free_resources.title: Lecture Archives
free_resources.description: Sunday talks by the resident and visiting swamis, listed by date and topic, many with video. Categories cover the Gita, the direct disciples of Ramakrishna and spiritual life.

free_resources.title: Sunday Worship, Talks and Weekday Classes
free_resources.description: The visiting page gives the weekly times: Sunday morning worship and a talk, plus evening classes on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday at the Carmichael temple. Open to all without charge.
